## Introduction

The STROBE (Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in
Epidemiology) statement asks observational studies to report how the study
population was selected, usually as a flow diagram. The
[`flowchart`](https://bruigtp.github.io/flowchart/) package on CRAN builds
that diagram while you build your cohort: each filtering step records how
many records were kept and how many were excluded.

This vignette shows how to:

1. Start a flow diagram from a loaded SRTR file
2. Apply inclusion criteria one at a time, with exclusion boxes
3. Draw and export the diagram
4. Get the final cohort back as a data frame

The code below needs your own SRTR files, so it is shown but not run.

## Setup

```{r setup, eval=FALSE}
install.packages("flowchart")

library(sRtr)
library(flowchart)

TX_KI <- load_srtr_file("TX_KI")
```

## Example: a kidney transplant cohort

`as_fc()` starts the diagram from a data frame. Each `fc_filter()` keeps the
rows where its condition is true; `show_exc = TRUE` adds a box counting the
rows it removed.

```{r basic_example, eval=FALSE}
kidney_fc <- TX_KI |>
  as_fc(label = "All kidney transplants") |>
  fc_filter(
    DON_AGE > 18,
    label = "Donor over 18 years old",
    show_exc = TRUE,
    label_exc = "Donor 18 or younger"
  ) |>
  fc_filter(
    DON_ABO == "B",
    label = "Donor blood type B",
    show_exc = TRUE,
    label_exc = "Donor blood type not B"
  ) |>
  fc_filter(
    REC_AGE >= 18 & REC_AGE <= 65,
    label = "Recipient age 18 to 65",
    show_exc = TRUE,
    label_exc = "Recipient age outside 18 to 65"
  )
```

Rows where a condition is `NA` (for example, a missing donor age) are
excluded, the same as in `dplyr::filter()`. If missing values should be
handled differently, recode them first, for example with
`srtr_normalize_missing()`.

## What the boxes count

`flowchart` counts rows. In `TX_KI` a row is a transplant, so a recipient
with two kidney transplants is counted twice; label the boxes as transplants,
or reduce to one row per recipient (for example on `PERS_ID`) as a labelled
step of its own. Build the diagram before joining files with many rows per
transplant, such as the follow-up file `TXF_KI`: after that join each row is
a follow-up form, and the counts no longer describe transplants.

## Drawing and exporting the diagram

```{r draw, eval=FALSE}
kidney_fc |>
  fc_draw()

kidney_fc |>
  fc_draw() |>
  fc_export("kidney-cohort.png", width = 3000, height = 4000, res = 700)
```

`fc_draw()` and `fc_filter()` have many arguments for box size, text and
color; see the [`flowchart` reference](https://bruigtp.github.io/flowchart/reference/index.html).

## Getting the cohort back

The flowchart object keeps the filtered data in its `data` element, so the
cohort used in the diagram is the cohort you analyze:

```{r cohort, eval=FALSE}
kidney_cohort <- kidney_fc$data
nrow(kidney_cohort)
```

The step-by-step counts behind the boxes are in `kidney_fc$fc`.
